title: Admin - Comment Moderation - Reject Content - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Comment Moderation - Reject Content feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Admins to reject inappropriate content (reviews, queries, vendor responses) to maintain platform standards. Covers reject action, status update, public visibility removal, optional rejection reason, action logging, and vendor/user notification.

testCases.title: Clicking Reject updates content status to Rejected
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item (review/query/vendor response) with 'Pending' or 'Needs Review' status exists in the moderation queue.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Identify a content card with pending/needs review status
Note the current status of the content item
Click the 'Reject' button on the content card
Observe the status change on the card
expectedResults: A 'Reject' button/action is visible on the content card
Clicking 'Reject' updates the content status to 'Rejected'
The status label on the card changes to reflect 'Rejected'
The status change is immediate without page reload
The card visually indicates the rejected state (e.g., color change, icon)
testCases.postconditions: Content item status is updated to Rejected in the system

testCases.title: Rejected content is not publicly visible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item has been rejected.
steps: Reject a content item (review/query/vendor response) from the moderation queue
Note the product/page associated with the rejected content
Open a new browser/incognito window as a regular (non-admin) user
Navigate to the product page where the rejected content was originally posted
Search for the rejected content text
expectedResults: The rejected content is NOT visible to public/regular users
The product page does not display the rejected review/query/response
No trace of the rejected content appears in the public-facing UI
Other approved content on the same page remains visible
The rejection effectively hides the content from all non-admin users
testCases.postconditions: Rejected content confirmed hidden from public view

testCases.title: Admin can provide optional rejection reason
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending content item exists in the moderation queue.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Find a content card with pending status
Click the 'Reject' button
Observe if a rejection reason input/dialog appears
Enter a rejection reason (e.g., 'Contains inappropriate language')
Confirm the rejection
expectedResults: After clicking Reject, an option to provide a reason is presented
The rejection reason field is optional (not mandatory)
Admin can type a free-text reason for rejection
The rejection proceeds successfully with the reason provided
The reason is saved and associated with the rejection action
testCases.postconditions: Content is rejected with the provided reason stored

testCases.title: Admin can reject content without providing a reason
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending content item exists in the moderation queue.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Find a content card with pending status
Click the 'Reject' button
If a reason dialog appears, leave the reason field empty
Confirm the rejection without entering a reason
expectedResults: The rejection proceeds successfully without a reason
No validation error is shown for empty reason field
The content status changes to 'Rejected'
The system does not force the admin to provide a reason
The rejection is recorded even without a reason
testCases.postconditions: Content is rejected without a reason

testCases.title: Rejection action is logged in the system
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending content item exists.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Note the admin's username/identity
Reject a content item
Check the content item's history/audit log (if accessible via UI)
Verify the rejection action is recorded
expectedResults: The rejection action is logged with timestamp
The log records which admin performed the rejection
The log includes the content item identifier
If a reason was provided, it is included in the log
The action log is accessible for audit purposes

testCases.title: Rejected content moves to Rejected status filter
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item has just been rejected.
steps: Reject a content item from the moderation queue
Note the content item details
Apply the 'Rejected' status filter
Search for the recently rejected item
expectedResults: The rejected item appears in the 'Rejected' status filter view
The item shows 'Rejected' status label
The rejection timestamp is visible
The item is no longer in the 'Pending' or 'Needs Review' filter
testCases.postconditions: Rejected content is correctly categorized under Rejected filter

testCases.title: Vendor/User notification on content rejection
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item from a known vendor/user exists in pending status.
steps: Reject a content item with a rejection reason
Check if the vendor/user receives a notification
Verify the notification contains the rejection reason
Check notification channel (email, in-app, or both)
expectedResults: The vendor/user is notified about the content rejection
The notification includes the rejection reason (if provided)
The notification identifies which content was rejected
The notification is sent through the appropriate channel
The notification is timely (sent shortly after rejection)
testCases.postconditions: Vendor/User has been notified of the rejection

testCases.title: Reject button is not available on already rejected content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item with 'Rejected' status exists.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Filter by 'Rejected' status
Find a previously rejected content card
Observe the available actions on the card
expectedResults: The 'Reject' button is NOT available on already rejected content
No duplicate rejection is possible
The card may show other actions (e.g., Approve to reverse decision) or no actions
The rejected status is clearly displayed

testCases.title: Reject button is not available on already approved content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item with 'Approved' status exists.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Filter by 'Approved' status
Find an approved content card
Observe the available actions on the card
expectedResults: The 'Reject' button is NOT available on already approved content (or if available, it allows status reversal)
The approved status is clearly displayed
If reject is available on approved content, it should require confirmation
testCases.postconditions: Confirmed behavior of reject on approved content

testCases.title: Multiple content items can be rejected in sequence
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Multiple pending content items exist in the moderation queue.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Reject the first pending content item
Verify the first item is rejected
Reject the second pending content item
Verify the second item is rejected
Reject the third pending content item
Verify the third item is rejected
expectedResults: Each rejection is processed independently and successfully
No errors occur when rejecting multiple items in sequence
Each rejected item's status updates correctly
The moderation queue updates after each rejection
Performance remains acceptable for sequential rejections
testCases.postconditions: Multiple items rejected successfully in sequence

testCases.title: Rejection reason with special characters is handled correctly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending content item exists.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Click Reject on a pending content item
Enter a rejection reason with special characters (e.g., '<script>alert(1)</script>', '"quotes"', 'emoji 🚫')
Confirm the rejection
Verify the reason is stored correctly
expectedResults: Special characters in the reason are handled safely (no XSS)
The reason is stored and displayed correctly
HTML/script tags are escaped or sanitized
Unicode characters and emojis are preserved
No application errors occur
testCases.postconditions: Rejection reason with special characters is safely stored

testCases.title: Rejection reason with maximum length boundary
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending content item exists.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Click Reject on a pending content item
Enter a very long rejection reason (500+ characters)
Attempt to confirm the rejection
Observe if there is a character limit or truncation
expectedResults: If a character limit exists, it is clearly communicated to the admin
The system either accepts the long reason or shows a validation message
No application crash or error occurs with long input
If truncated, the admin is informed before submission
testCases.postconditions: Boundary behavior for rejection reason length is confirmed

testCases.title: Page refresh after rejection retains the rejected status
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A content item has just been rejected.
steps: Reject a content item
Note the content item details
Refresh the page (F5 or browser reload)
Navigate back to the moderation queue
Search for the rejected item
expectedResults: After page refresh, the rejected status persists
The item does not revert to pending status
The rejection is permanently stored in the database
The item appears under 'Rejected' filter after refresh
testCases.postconditions: Rejection persistence confirmed after page refresh

testCases.title: AI-flagged content can be rejected by admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content flagged by AI (offensive/spam/negative sentiment) exists in moderation.
steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
Find a content item flagged by AI moderation
Observe the AI flagging indicators (Device Matcher Notes, badges)
Click 'Reject' on the AI-flagged content
Confirm the rejection
expectedResults: AI-flagged content has the Reject action available
The rejection works the same as for non-flagged content
The AI flags are preserved in the rejection record
The content status changes to Rejected
The AI flagging aids the admin's decision but doesn't auto-reject
testCases.postconditions: AI-flagged content rejected by admin action

testCases.title: Vendor-flagged content can be rejected by admin

steps: Navigate to Comment Moderation page
